data.cultural_impact: The name "Umran" holds a deep cultural significance for the Islamic community, as it is a nomenclature that is synonymous with the religious pilgrimage to Mecca. Umrah, being the lesser pilgrimage, is one of the Five Pillars of Islam and is undertaken by millions of Muslims every year. The name acts as a constant reminder of one's faith, commitment, and devotion to their religion.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Umran" represents a journey towards seeking a deeper and more meaningful connection with the Almighty. It implies an individual who has embarked on a physical and spiritual journey to the holy city of Mecca, experiencing self-reflection and augmenting their faith through acts of worship. This name signifies a dedication to upholding the tenets of the Islamic faith and maintaining a constant remembrance of Allah in one's daily life.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Ibn Sa'd, Al-Tabaqat Al-Kubra, Vol. 1, p. 189-190. Umran ibn Al-Aswad Al-Fihri was a companion of Prophet Muhammad and one of the leaders of the Ansar (Helpers) of Medina. He was also known as Umran ibn Al-Mugheerah Al-Makhzumi, and was a cousin of Ali ibn Abi Talib. Umran played a significant role in the Battle of Uhud (625 CE), where he fought bravely and was one of the few companions who remained with the Prophet when the Muslim army was defeated and retreated back to Medina.
historical_references.context: Battle of Uhud, Companion of Prophet Muhammad, Leader of Ansar, Cousin of Ali ibn Abi Talib

historical_references.reference: Ibn Hisham, Sirat Rasul Allah, p. 547-548. Umran ibn Al-Asad Al-Fihri was a prominent companion of Prophet Muhammad and a leader of the Ansar. He was also known as Umran ibn Al-Mugheerah Al-Makhzumi. Umran played a crucial role in the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (628 CE) by negotiating with the Meccan delegation and ensuring the safe return of Muslim pilgrims who had gone to Mecca for Hajj.
historical_references.context: Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, Negotiator with Meccan delegation, Companion of Prophet Muhammad, Leader of Ansar
